title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
blurb: Found that model size and training tokens should scale roughly equally with compute, about 20 tokens per parameter, and showed a smaller model trained on more data beats a larger undertrained one.
intro: The paper trains hundreds of models across sizes and token counts and estimates the compute-optimal split three ways: from the lower envelope of training curves, from IsoFLOP profiles, and from a parametric fit $L = E + A/N^\alpha + B/D^\beta$. The steps build FLOP counting, compute budgets, power-law fits with and without a loss floor, the IsoFLOP exponent and allocation rules; the capstone fits the parametric loss and derives the optimal model and data size for several budgets.
